clue.text: Nation excited with charmer like Justin Trudeau

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A whole country is thrilled by a charming politician, the way Canadians once swooned over Justin Trudeau.
explanation.definitionFit: Trudeau was Prime Minister of Canada, a country on that continent, so the phrase describes someone from there.

clue.text: Declines surgery: pets only half sedated

indicators.note: only half of the word survives, so the front two letters are dropped

parts.note: an op is an operation, a piece of surgery
taken as written before it is cut down
someone sedated is out cold

explanation.surface: An owner refuses an operation because the vet's sedation only half worked on the animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the back half of pets is kept, so OP + TS + OUT gives OPTS OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose not to take part, which is a way of turning something down.

clue.text: 72 hours or so ago, child born then has far to go

definitions.meaning: first meaning: if today is Sunday, the day roughly three days back

definitions.text: child born then has far to go
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the nursery rhyme Monday's Child says this day's child has far to go

explanation.walkthrough: The old rhyme 'Monday's child is fair of face' gives each weekday's child a trait, and the one with far to go is THURSDAY's.
explanation.definitionFit: Counted back from a weekend day, three days earlier lands on this weekday, used adverbially as in 'I saw her Thursday'.

clue.text: Does away with lines on a graph

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cuts or scraps, as a firm cuts jobs
second meaning: the plural of axis, the reference lines of a chart

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are pronounced differently: the verb rhymes with taxes, the plural of axis ends in a long 'eez' sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe something is to cancel or eliminate it, and the horizontal and vertical reference lines of a chart are its axes.

clue.text: Old, anguished, wretched: there's nothing to add

indicators.note: something wretched is in a sorry, broken state, so these letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone elderly and miserable sums up their plight and declares the conversation over.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom closes a discussion by declaring the point fully made, so no further words are needed.

clue.text: Criminal lawyer hides after considering everything

indicators.note: the phrase keeps the letters concealed inside itself, straddling the two words

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A crooked lawyer goes to ground once they've weighed up all the options.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means taking every item together, as in a total or overall view of matters.

clue.text: In AA, I mean to raise condition

indicators.note: to raise is to stir up or rouse, so the letters are disturbed into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters taken as written, ignoring the punctuation

explanation.surface: At an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting, someone says they intend to bring up a medical problem.
explanation.walkthrough: AA reads as Alcoholics Anonymous, but here it is just two letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemia is a medical disorder, a shortage of red blood cells, and condition is the usual word for an illness.

clue.text: Direction borders on conservative in Romeo and Juliet adaptation

parts.note: a compass direction
edges or borders
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A stage director's take on Shakespeare's tragedy edges towards a conservative reading.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' means the piece placed after, below the earlier pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bernstein musical relocates Shakespeare's star-crossed lovers to rival New York gangs, a famous reworking of the play.

clue.text: Pursuit in which diet is foiled?

definitions.text: Pursuit in which diet is foiled?

parts.words: Pursuit in which diet is foiled?
parts.note: surface reading: some activity that wrecks a slimming plan
setter's reading: a children's search for chocolate treats wrapped in foil each spring, ruinous to any diet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Foiled' means thwarted on the surface, but the chocolate being sought is literally wrapped in foil.
explanation.definitionFit: Children search a garden for hidden chocolate treats at the spring festival, a hunt being a pursuit.

clue.text: Umpteenth US evangelical stifles praise

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother and hold something inside, so the letters lie within the phrase

parts.note: found running across the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Yet another American preacher suppresses words of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthuse is to speak with eager admiration, and to praise is to speak warmly of something, close verbs.

clue.text: Local's stripped down to nothing in Spain, giving patriotic song

indicators.note: stripping takes off the outer covering, so the end letters go and the inside is kept

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters removed
nada is Spanish for nothing

explanation.surface: A native is reduced to nothing on a Spanish trip, yet bursts into a national anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Canada's national anthem, a song sung to express love of one's country.

clue.text: Illicitly loots workman's implements

indicators.note: doing something illicitly bends the rules, so the letters are rearranged out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone unlawfully steals a tradesman's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammers, saws and spanners are the hand implements a craftsman works with, the general word for them.

clue.text: Time lag I suffered to overcome this?

definitions.text: Time lag I suffered to overcome this?

indicators.note: something that has suffered has been knocked about, so these letters are battered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains they had to wait out a delay before they were old enough for something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes waiting for the years to pass until you are allowed in, which is what the letters spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A minimum age rule is overcome only by the passing of time, so a lag you endure gets you past it.

clue.text: Measure that monitors monitors?

parts.note: surface reading: a gadget checking computer displays
setter's reading: a tally of the hours spent looking at phones and computer displays

explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word flips from verb (keeps watch on) to noun (displays), so the measure tracks time spent at displays.
explanation.definitionFit: Phones report how many hours a day someone spends looking at devices, a measure that keeps watch on use of displays.

clue.text: Nervously hint at lawsuit, then

indicators.note: done nervously means done jitteringly, so the letters shake into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a case is a lawsuit brought before a court

explanation.surface: Someone timidly mentions the possibility of legal action, and then draws a conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions draw a consequence from what was just said, meaning 'if so' or 'accordingly'.

clue.text: Former prime minister — no leader — in retreat

indicators.note: with no leader the word loses its first letter

parts.note: Tony Blair, UK Prime Minister 1997 to 2007

explanation.surface: An ex-premier, out of power, has gone into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is an animal's den or a hiding place, somewhere one withdraws to, which is a sense of retreat.

clue.text: Zane's gutted, with chafed nipple in airship

indicators.note: something chafed is rubbed raw and roughed up, so the letters are rearranged
gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A distressed passenger called Zane suffers a sore chest on a long airship flight.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored: Zane gutted keeps Z and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeppelins were the rigid German dirigibles of the early twentieth century, the best-known kind of airship.

clue.text: Teas consumed?

indicators.note: something consumed is broken down and eaten up, so its letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, afternoon teas that get eaten are food, and the letters of teas reshuffle to the informal word for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal slang for food, and teas served and consumed are exactly that.

clue.text: A billion tacos cooked with this condiment?

indicators.note: cooked food is transformed in the pan, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
B is a standard abbreviation for billion
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone makes an enormous number of tacos and asks if this sauce goes on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a brand of fiery red pepper sauce added to food at table, which makes it a condiment.

clue.text: Deign to advance one letter, with organ enclosed in posting

indicators.note: something enclosed is shut inside, so one piece goes within the other
one letter is pushed forward a place, which rearranges the word

parts.note: taken as written
the liver is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: A haughty postman condescends to send on a letter containing an organ donor card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One letter' is not post but a single letter of the word, which shifts one place towards the end before the organ goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Posting a parcel or letter means sending it, and delivering is handing the item over to its destination.

clue.text: Suppose I'm a gin enthusiast primarily

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone tentatively admits they are mainly a gin lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine something is to assume or picture it as so, close in meaning to supposing it.

clue.text: Mountain folk live among giants

indicators.note: among means surrounded by, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the Titans were giant gods of Greek myth
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Hill people dwell among a race of giants, as in some folk tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet sits on the high Himalayan plateau, so its people are a highland, mountain-dwelling nation.

clue.text: Playing whist, void of hearts, trump's opening: another card, please

indicators.note: playing with letters moves them about into a fresh arrangement
in card shorthand hearts is H, and void of means lacking, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter

indicators.note: an opening is the very start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A card player with no hearts in hand leads a trump and asks the dealer for another card.
explanation.walkthrough: In pontoon (the British name for blackjack), you say 'twist' to be dealt another card. A suit you hold no cards in is a void.
explanation.definitionFit: In pontoon, the British version of blackjack, saying this word asks the dealer for one more card.

clue.text: American poet finds path around lake

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece is wrapped about the other

parts.note: taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A poet out walking discovers a trail circling a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvia Plath, author of Ariel and The Bell Jar, was a celebrated poet born in Boston.

clue.text: Suitor that's utterly desirable at first?

definitions.text: Suitor that's utterly desirable at first?

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A wooer is irresistibly attractive, at least on first impressions.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a very attractive man courting someone, which is also what the initials spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the word for a sexually attractive young man, a fitting description of an irresistible admirer.

clue.text: Composer with some dross in Italian

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters are a part taken from inside the phrase

parts.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: A composer whose work contains some rubbish, written in Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian' looks like a hint that the composer is Italian, which he is, but here it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini wrote The Barber of Seville and William Tell, operas by an Italian composer.

clue.text: To make up story about king, head of Númenor: this author did!

definitions.text: To make up story about king, head of Númenor: this author did!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to lie is to make up a story
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the head is the top, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A fan marvels that one writer invented a royal saga set in his own fantasy island kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Númenor is an island kingdom in Middle-earth, and The Return of the King is the final Lord of the Rings volume, so the whole clue describes the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: J.R.R. Tolkien invented Middle-earth and Númenor and wrote The Return of the King, literally making up a story about a king.

clue.text: Rising sun soon heated coastal resort

indicators.note: heated things are agitated and excited, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, also part of the letters

explanation.surface: The sun comes up and quickly warms a seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Southend-on-Sea is an Essex seaside town on the Thames estuary, popular with London day trippers.
